description: Per-character shikigami sets: ordered lists of ShikigamiDataTable character IDs that a character can summon or pose in battles, cutscenes and UI captures.

ID.simple: Row key referenced by Character::Id_CharacterShikigami entries.
ID.technical: FName primary key (ImportKeyField=Id in the export). Battle asset collection and battle/level-sequence setup iterate the character's Id_CharacterShikigami set IDs, skip None and resolve each via CharacterShikigamiDataTables (DTM +0x4F0).

Id_Shikigami.simple: Ordered list of shikigami character IDs belonging to this set.
Id_Shikigami.technical: TArray<FName>, up to nine slots in the export. The asset collector walks the list, skips None, resolves each Shikigami row (DTM +0x6C0), appends its FileName_BP and expands its Id_ShikigamiAnimation rows' FileName arrays into preload lists. BattleBase spawns each listed shikigami from its loaded FileName_BP class and installs its montages; LevelSequencer resolves the same rows for sequence setup. Duplicate IDs in a set are preserved (e.g. CP_120 repeats CN_050), so slots are meaningful and not deduplicated here.

notes: Export contains 10 rows, uniformly with nine Id_Shikigami slots; unused slots are None.
This table stores only the shikigami ID list; actual Blueprint names, animation IDs and stats live in ShikigamiDataTable and related tables.
The same set is also consulted independently by capture code only when a CharacterCapture row has a non-None Id_ShikigamiCharacter; capture does not read this table directly.
Single table asset 'CharacterShikigamiDataTable' loaded into DTM +0x4F0; no numbered shards or localization variants in the export.
Reconstructed source with cited retail RVAs; no claim about Blueprint-only uses or byte-identical matching.

usages.detail: Resolves each shikigami set and collects shikigami Blueprints and animations into preload lists.
Battle setup resolves the set and spawns the listed shikigami.
Level-sequencer setup resolves the same set for cutscene shikigami.
